title: Xanthe and the Terminal
premise: Sebastian Zhou smuggles memories—recorded human experience—past orbital customs in sealed neural drives, scraping a living between the mining colony of Kestrel's Landing and the core worlds. When the colony is quietly destroyed in an 'industrial accident' and every official record of it vanishes, Sebastian realizes the only surviving proof is the contraband memories they've been carrying for years: thousands of ordinary lives, including those of Xanthe Reyes, the customs officer who loved them and died trying to warn them. Hunted by the corporation that erased Kestrel's Landing, Sebastian must piece together a testimony from fragments of other people's pasts, risking everything to broadcast the massacre before their own memory can be seized and rewritten. In the end, Sebastian sacrifices their anonymity—and nearly their identity—to make the colony's death unforgettable, carrying Xanthe's final recording into the public record at terrible personal cost.
about_author: Sable Okonkwo is a former maritime radio operator turned science fiction writer whose work explores memory, migration, and the people history misfiles. They live between coastal cities and write on ships whenever they can.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs introduces Sebastian's trade in contraband memories and their careful invisibility. A near-inspection forces them to destroy one drive—an old woman's wedding—and the loss stings more than it should. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Cross-checking ledgers, Sebastian finds a ship on a decade-old manifest—the Meridian—that never flew, listing a passenger named Xanthe Reyes they've never heard of. The record should not exist. Emotional beat: the first crack in a carefully managed life.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Landing
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with embedded memory-fragments. Flashback chapters show the colony as Sebastian knew it: dust, oxygen rationing, a bar called the Last Chance where everyone owed everyone money. Emotional beat: nostalgia curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Customs Officer Reyes
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV (recovered recording). Years earlier, Xanthe waves Sebastian through customs while quietly logging their smuggling—not to prosecute, but because she's fascinated by what people choose to remember. Their flirtation begins across a scanner bed. Emotional beat: cautious tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Drives Carry
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Inventorying stock, Sebastian discovers several drives contain footage from Kestrel's Landing dated after its supposed destruction—including a child's birthday party recorded three days after the 'accident.' Emotional beat: vertigo; the timeline is wrong.

chapters.title: The Erasure
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Official channels confirm Kestrel's Landing never existed; debts, birth records, shipping histories—all scrubbed. Sebastian's own childhood there is now legally impossible. Emotional beat: gaslighting at civilizational scale.

chapters.title: Buyer's Market
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A wealthy collector offers a fortune for 'pre-erasure colonial ephemera,' revealing that someone is buying up and destroying every trace of the colony. Taking the meeting means exposing himself. Emotional beat: temptation versus conscience.

chapters.title: Xanthe's Warning
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV (final recording). Hidden in a drive Sebastian has carried for years, Xanthe explains she found the corporate order for the colony's termination and started copying evidence into smuggled memory-drives—Sebastian's own cargo was her dead-drop. She names the ship that never flew. Emotional beat: love revealed too late.

chapters.title: Hollow Orbit
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Returning to Kestrel's Landing's coordinates, Sebastian finds only a scoured rock and a corporate salvage rig stripping the debris field. They narrowly evade detection but capture a fragment of the rig's own sensor logs. Emotional beat: grief made physical.

chapters.title: The Collector's Vault
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Breaking into the collector's vault, Sebastian finds shelves of seized drives—memories confiscated from colonists before the end. Among them, dozens labeled R., XAN. Emotional beat: horror and resolve intertwined.

chapters.title: Reading the Dead
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sebastian experiences Xanthe's drives: her childhood, her recruitment by customs, her growing suspicion of her employers. Each memory deepens both the case and Sebastian's love for someone already gone. Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Corporate security finally makes Sebastian—they were always on file from customs scans. A chase through the station's underdecks costs Sebastian their ship and half their inventory. Emotional beat: paranoia becoming certainty.

chapters.title: Alibi of Ash
chapters.summary: Corporate antagonist Voss's POV. Voss explains, reasonably, why erasure was cheaper than evacuation: the colony's debt exceeded its value. He offers Sebastian restoration of their records in exchange for the drives. Emotional beat: banality of evil.

chapters.title: The Witness Problem
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Memories aren't admissible evidence; courts call them 'subjective artifacts.' Sebastian seeks a retired judge living off-grid who once ruled on neural testimony. Emotional beat: the law itself feels like an enemy.

chapters.title: Precedent
chapters.summary: Judge Amara Osei's POV. Osei agrees the memories could constitute testimony—if a living witness will bind themselves to them, accepting legal ownership of the trauma. She warns Sebastian what that means. Emotional beat: the price named aloud.

chapters.title: Loading Xanthe
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Preparing to merge Xanthe's recordings with their own memory, Sebastian says goodbye to their anonymity, their aliases, their clean record. The procedure begins. Emotional beat: willing self-destruction for truth.

chapters.title: Two Lives, One Skull
chapters.summary: Blended POV. Post-merge, Sebastian carries Xanthe's memories natively—her voice in their recall, her death replaying unbidden. Identity frays at the seams. Emotional beat: love as burden, memory as wound.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian hijacks the corporation's own ceremonial uplink during a shareholder address, streaming the merged testimony—massacre, cover-up, manifest—to every screen in the system. Security closes in. Emotional beat: triumph and terror at once.

chapters.title: Voss Descending
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, then Sebastian's. Voss attempts to seize Sebastian and 'correct' their memory in custody; the public broadcast makes him hesitate, then overreach, ordering a wipe on camera. His own officers refuse. Emotional beat: the machine turning on its hand.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In court, Sebastian testifies as witness for the dead, memories verified against recovered physical wreckage from the salvage rig. The verdict: Kestrel's Landing existed; the massacre happened. Emotional beat: justice arriving battered but real.

chapters.title: What Remains of Me
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Legally restored but internally changed, Sebastian can no longer fully distinguish which griefs are theirs. They keep Xanthe's memories rather than have them excised, choosing to carry her. Emotional beat: mourning as devotion.

chapters.title: Manifest, Corrected
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At a rebuilt memorial dock, Sebastian files the Meridian's true flight log with Xanthe listed among the passengers who never flew—and boards a ship out, finally visible, finally known. Emotional beat: survival as remembrance, departure as beginning.
